mainTopic: Counting and judging sightings of blood: a young girl's כתם and flows, checking girls, and how far a pregnant or nursing woman's דיה שעתה extends.
overview: This amud deals with how to count and judge sightings of blood in several special cases. It opens with רבי אלעאי challenging חזקיה's ruling that a young girl's כתם is טמא, and רבי זירא defends it: a newly married בתולה often bleeds from her wound, but a young girl does not. עולא then quotes רבי יוחנן in the name of רבי שמעון בן יהוצדק that such a girl's spit, מדרס and כתם are all טהור, and רבין's report shows that חזקיה stands alone against two. Next, רב חלקיה בר טובי teaches that seven days of nonstop flow count as one sighting, and after re-reading רב שימי בר חייא's words, that dripping counts the same as nonstop flow. A ברייתא sets the default status of girls before and after maturity, and רבי יהודה explains a gentle way to check them. The גמרא then turns to רבי יוסי's ruling in the משנה and shows that a woman's missed cycles during pregnancy and during nursing combine to make three. Finally, רב and ריש לקיש argue with שמואל and רבי יוחנן about whether the limit of דיה שעתה to the first sighting covers all four women in the משנה. The גמרא begins to link this argument to a dispute between תנאים, and the quote continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Why is a young girl different from a newly married virgin?
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעאי challenges חזקיה's ruling that the young girl's כתם is טמא, comparing her to a בתולה whose stains are טהור.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעאי challenged this: What is the difference between this girl and a בתולה, whose blood is treated as pure?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעאי attacks the ruling from just before this, where חזקיה said a young girl who saw blood twice has a טמא כתם. He points to a similar case where we are lenient.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a newly married בתולה, we assume the blood comes from her wound and not from נדה, so her stains are טהור. רבי אלעאי asks why we don't make the same assumption for a young girl who is not yet expected to see blood. If both are cases of 'blood that may not be נדה blood,' they should have the same law.

keyTerms.meaning: challenged it; a strong objection to a ruling
a virgin; here, a newly married girl who bleeds from her wound
her blood is pure; for a set period, her blood is assumed not to be נדה blood

phrases.english: Rabbi Ilai objected to it:
phrases.notes: "It" is חזקיה's ruling from just before, that the young girl's stain is impure.

phrases.english: And what is the difference between this one
and a virgin whose blood is pure?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges חזקיה's ruling, stated earlier on the daf.
steps.kashyaTarget: חזקיה's ruling that a young girl who saw blood twice has a טמא כתם.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A comparison case: a בתולה's stains are treated as טהור because the blood may not be נדה blood. The same reasoning should apply to the young girl.

steps.title: The virgin's bleeding is common; the girl's is not
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא explains that a בתולה commonly bleeds from her wound, so we can blame stains on that. A young girl has no such common source of blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said to him: This one (the בתולה) commonly has wound-bleeding, and this one (the young girl) does not commonly have it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא defends חזקיה. He shows that the two cases are not really the same.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The leniency for a בתולה works only because there is a known, frequent source of non-נדה blood: her wound. A young girl has no such regular source. So if blood is found on her, the likely explanation is that it is נדה blood.

keyTerms.meaning: her secretion; here, bleeding from the wound, not נדה blood
common, frequently found

steps.whatToRemember: We can blame a stain on another source only when that source is common. A בתולה has one, but a young girl does not, so חזקיה's ruling stands.

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said to him:
This one, her secretion is common,
phrases.notes: "This one" is the newly married virgin, whose wound bleeds regularly.

phrases.english: and this one, her secretion is not common.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי אלעאי's challenge by showing the two cases differ.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A young girl and a בתולה are alike, since both may have blood that is not נדה blood.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only the בתולה has a common, known source of other blood, so only her stains can be assumed טהור.

steps.title: A ruling that the young girl's stain is pure
steps.stepSummary: עולא quotes רבי יוחנן in the name of רבי שמעון בן יהוצדק: a young girl who saw blood once or twice has spit, מדרס, and כתם that are all טהור. עולא is unsure whose words the כתם part is.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said in the name of רבי יוחנן, who said it in the name of רבי שמעון בן יהוצדק: A young girl whose time to see blood has not come, and who saw blood a first and second time, has spit and מדרס found in the market that are טהור. Her כתם is also טהור. עולא added: I don't know if this is רבי יוחנן's own view or his teacher's.
steps.whatsHappening: A new statement is brought that goes against חזקיה: the young girl's כתם is טהור. עולא admits he is not sure who said the כתם part.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since she has not yet seen three times, she is not considered a woman who regularly sees blood. So things found in the market that might be hers are not assumed טמא. This ruling stretches that leniency to her כתם too, which directly disagrees with חזקיה. עולא is unsure whether the כתם ruling comes from רבי יוחנן alone or also from his teacher. Step 6 settles this.

keyTerms.meaning: a young girl
saliva, spit
something she treads or sits on, which can become טמא from her
a blood stain found on a garment or body
his own / his teacher's

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two parts. The spit and מדרס ruling is not in doubt. עולא's uncertainty is only about the added line 'כתמה נמי טהור': did רבי יוחנן add it himself, or did he get it from רבי שמעון בן יהוצדק?

phrases.english: Ulla said: Rabbi Yochanan said
in the name of Rabbi Shimon ben Yehotzadak:
A young girl whose time to see blood has not arrived,
and she saw a first and second time —
her saliva and her trodden item in the marketplace are pure,
her stain is also pure.

phrases.aramaic: וְלָא יָדַעְנָא אִם דִּידֵיהּ, אִם דְּרַבֵּיהּ.
phrases.english: And I do not know if it is his own, or his teacher's.
phrases.notes: This is עולא speaking. He isn't sure if the stain part is רבי יוחנן's own or רבי שמעון בן יהוצדק's.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר עוּלָּא, אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יְהוֹצָדָק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings an opinion that disagrees with חזקיה's ruling, which was just defended.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A young girl who saw blood only once or twice has spit, מדרס, and כתם that are all טהור.

steps.title: Why does it matter who said it?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what practical difference there is whether the ruling is רבי יוחנן's own or his teacher's.
steps.simpleTranslation: What difference does it make?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions עולא's doubt. If the law is the same either way, why care who said it? This sets up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The content of the ruling does not change based on who said it. So the גמרא wants to know what real result depends on the name attached to it.

keyTerms.meaning: practical difference; what comes out of it

phrases.english: For what does it make a difference?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about עולא's uncertainty from the previous step.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What practical result depends on whether the כתם ruling is רבי יוחנן's or his teacher's?

steps.title: One opinion against two
steps.stepSummary: The difference is about the count of opinions. If both רבי יוחנן and his teacher said it, then חזקיה is one against two.
steps.simpleTranslation: So that it will be the words of one against two.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that it matters for counting opinions. It decides whether חזקיה is a lone voice against two Sages.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the כתם ruling is from רבי שמעון בן יהוצדק and רבי יוחנן repeats it, then two Sages say טהור and only חזקיה says טמא. Normally we do not follow one against two. If it is only רבי יוחנן's view, it is one against one.

keyTerms.meaning: the words of one Sage against two, a minority view

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that knowing exactly who said a ruling can decide the הלכה, since a single opinion usually does not win against two.

phrases.english: For it to be the words of one
in the place of two.
phrases.notes: The "one" is חזקיה, standing against רבי יוחנן and his teacher.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמִיהְוֵי דְּבָרָיו שֶׁל אֶחָד בִּמְקוֹם שְׁנַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of the previous step.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It decides whether חזקיה's opinion stands alone against two Sages, which affects the הלכה.

steps.title: The travelers report it was the teacher's ruling
steps.stepSummary: When רבין and the sea travelers came from ארץ ישראל, they quoted this ruling in the name of רבי שמעון בן יהוצדק.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבין came, along with all the sea travelers, they said it in the name of רבי שמעון בן יהוצדק.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא's doubt is settled. The reports from ארץ ישראל say the ruling, including the כתם part, comes from רבי שמעון בן יהוצדק himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the teacher said it and רבי יוחנן repeated it, two Sages hold that the כתם is טהור. That makes חזקיה the single opinion against two.

keyTerms.meaning: sea travelers; Sages who brought teachings from ארץ ישראל to בבל
they said it, they reported it

steps.whatToRemember: The young girl's כתם is טהור in the view of both רבי שמעון בן יהוצדק and רבי יוחנן. So חזקיה, who called it טמא, is one against two.

phrases.english: When Ravin came
and all the seafarers,
they said it as Rabbi Shimon ben Yehotzadak.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אֲתָא רָבִין וְכֹל נָחוֹתֵי יַמָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Settles the uncertainty whose importance was just explained.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The ruling that the young girl's כתם is טהור belongs to רבי שמעון בן יהוצדק, and רבי יוחנן repeated it, so חזקיה is one against two.

steps.title: Seven days of continuous flow count as one sighting
steps.stepSummary: רב חלקיה בר טובי rules that a young girl not yet of age who flows continuously for seven days has had only one sighting, 'even' in that case.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חלקיה בר טובי said: a young girl who is not yet old enough to see blood, even if she bleeds nonstop for all seven days, has only had one sighting.
steps.whatsHappening: A new teacher, רב חלקיה בר טובי, tells us how to count sightings for a young girl. A long nonstop flow counts as just one sighting.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We just learned that a young girl who saw once or twice keeps lenient rulings, so the number of sightings matters. רב חלקיה בר טובי says one long unbroken flow, even for seven days, is still only one sighting. His word 'even' will be questioned in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: A young girl
Whose time to see blood has not yet come, meaning she is not yet of age
Flowing continuously, without stopping
All seven days of a usual period
One sighting of blood

phrases.english: Rav Ḥilkiya bar Tovi said:
A young girl whose time to see blood has not arrived,
even if she flows continuously all seven days,
it is only one sighting.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a new ruling on how to count sightings, which matters for the earlier 'once or twice' ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A young girl not yet of age who flows continuously for seven days has had only one sighting.

steps.title: The word 'even' makes no sense
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the word 'even'. It suggests that a flow that stops and starts is an easier case, but stopping and starting should count as two sightings.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why say 'even if she flows nonstop', as if it is obvious when she stops? The opposite is true: if she stops and starts again, that counts like two sightings!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the wording of רב חלקיה בר טובי. 'Even' suggests the stop-and-start case is more obvious, but logically it is the stricter case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying 'even X' means X is the harder case and the other case is easier. But a flow that stops and then restarts looks like two separate events, so it should count as two sightings. Nonstop flow is the easy case for 'one sighting', not the hard one.

keyTerms.meaning: Even (implies this is the harder case)
It is not even necessary to say
A flow that stops and then starts again
On the contrary, the opposite is true
Like two sightings

phrases.english: "Even" if she flows continuously,
and it is not even necessary to say if she stops?

phrases.aramaic: אַדְּרַבָּה, פּוֹסֶקֶת הָוְיָא לַהּ כִּשְׁתֵּי רְאִיּוֹת!
phrases.english: On the contrary, if she stops, it is like two sightings!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the wording of step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: The word 'even' in רב חלקיה בר טובי's statement.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'Even' implies stop-and-start is the easier case, but stop-and-start should count as two sightings, so it is actually the stricter case.

steps.title: Read the statement without 'even'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא re-reads רב חלקיה בר טובי's statement without 'even': if she flows continuously for seven days, it is one sighting.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say: a young girl not yet of age who flows nonstop for all seven days has had only one sighting.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the wording by dropping 'even'. The ruling now only talks about nonstop flow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without 'even', there is no hint that a stop-and-start flow is also one sighting. The ruling is simply that a nonstop flow, however long, is one sighting. The case of stopping and starting is left as counting more.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (introduces a corrected reading)
And she flows continuously (the plain 'and' replaces 'even')

steps.whatToRemember: Nonstop flow, even for seven days, is one sighting. Stopping and starting again counts as more than one.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא, תִּינוֹקֶת שֶׁלֹּא הִגִּיעַ זְמַנָּהּ לִרְאוֹת,
phrases.english: Rather: a young girl whose time to see blood has not arrived,
and she flows continuously all seven days,
phrases.notes: Notice the word 'even' is gone. That is the whole fix.

phrases.english: it is only one sighting.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, תִּינוֹקֶת שֶׁלֹּא הִגִּיעַ זְמַנָּהּ לִרְאוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 8 by removing the troublesome word.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading the wording of the statement
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The statement said 'even', suggesting stop-and-start is also one sighting.
steps.terutzMaskana: The statement has no 'even'. Only nonstop flow is one sighting.

steps.title: A dripping woman is not like one who sees
steps.stepSummary: רב שימי בר חייא says a woman who drips blood (מדלפת) is not considered like one who sees.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שימי בר חייא said: a woman who drips blood is not considered like a woman who sees blood.
steps.whatsHappening: A new teacher brings a ruling about a woman whose blood comes out in drips. The next step will question it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a new type of flow: not a steady stream, but drip after drip. Read plainly, he says dripping does not count as seeing at all. The גמרא will find that hard to accept.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman whose blood comes out in drips
Like one who sees blood

phrases.english: Rav Shimi bar Ḥiyya said:
A woman who drips is not like one who sees,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a new case, dripping, to the discussion of how flows are counted.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A dripping woman is not like one who sees.

steps.title: But she did see blood
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: a dripping woman obviously did see blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: But she is seeing blood!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב שימי בר חייא: how can you say she did not 'see'? The blood is right there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Drips are real blood, so it makes no sense to say she is not like one who sees. The plain reading of the ruling cannot be right, and the next step will re-read it.

keyTerms.meaning: But surely (opens a challenge)
She is seeing (blood)

phrases.english: But she is seeing!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the plain meaning of step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that a dripping woman is not like one who sees.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: She clearly sees blood, so she must count as seeing.

steps.title: Dripping is like stopping and starting
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא re-reads the statement: dripping is not like continuous flow but like a flow that stops and starts.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say instead: she is not like a woman who flows nonstop, but like a woman whose flow stops and starts.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא changes what רב שימי בר חייא meant. He was not saying she did not see. He was saying which kind of seeing it is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now 'not like one who sees' means 'not like a nonstop flow'. Each drip is separate, like a stop-and-start flow. That would make dripping count as more than one sighting, which is a stricter result.

keyTerms.meaning: Say (read the statement this way instead)
Like a woman whose flow stops and starts

phrases.english: Say: she is not like one who flows continuously,
but like one who stops.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 11 by re-reading רב שימי בר חייא's words.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading the wording of the statement
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Dripping does not count as seeing at all.
steps.terutzMaskana: Dripping counts like a stop-and-start flow, not like a nonstop flow.

steps.title: Does a continuous flow run like a river?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: if dripping is not 'continuous', then continuous flow would have to mean a nonstop river of blood, which does not happen.
steps.simpleTranslation: That would mean a woman who 'flows continuously' must flow like a river?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the new reading from step 12. If drips break the flow, then 'continuous flow' would require a nonstop stream.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Real bleeding is never a perfect nonstop stream; it always comes somewhat in drips. If drips count as stopping, then nobody would ever count as שופעת. That cannot be what the term means.

keyTerms.meaning: From this it follows that
Like a river
Also

phrases.english: From this it follows that one who flows continuously
(also) flows like a river?
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets and some leave it out; the meaning stays the same.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that dripping is like stopping and starting.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If drips break a flow, then continuous flow would have to be a nonstop river, which is unrealistic.

steps.title: Dripping is just like continuous flow
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives a final reading: a dripping woman is treated exactly like one who flows continuously.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say: she is nothing other than like a woman who flows continuously.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles what רב שימי בר חייא meant. Dripping is the same as continuous flow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since continuous flow naturally comes in drips, dripping cannot be treated differently. So dripping counts as one long sighting, just like the seven days of flow in רב חלקיה בר טובי's ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: She is nothing other than
Like one who flows continuously

steps.whatToRemember: Dripping (מדלפת) counts the same as continuous flow (שופעת): one sighting. Only a flow that truly stops and starts again (פוסקת) counts as more.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the three readings of רב שימי בר חייא. The first reading (not seeing) and the second (like stopping) were both rejected. The final reading is: dripping is like continuous flow.
steps.whyThisMatters: This tells us how to count sightings for a young girl, which decides how long she keeps the lenient status from the earlier ruling.

phrases.english: Rather, say:
she is nothing other than like one who flows continuously.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 13 with a final reading of רב שימי בר חייא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading the wording of the statement
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Dripping is like stopping and starting.
steps.terutzMaskana: Dripping is exactly like continuous flow and counts as one sighting.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A dripping woman is treated like one who flows continuously: it is all one sighting.

steps.title: Young girls: presumed pure before maturity, presumed impure after
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that girls who have not reached maturity are in חזקת טהרה and need no checking. Once they reach maturity they are in חזקת טומאה and the women must check them.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: Jewish girls are presumed pure until they reach maturity, and the women do not need to check them. Once they reach maturity, they are presumed impure, and the women check them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic with a ברייתא. It sets the default status of a young girl based on whether she has reached physical maturity.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before maturity a girl is not expected to see blood, so we assume she is טהורה. Once she matures, an unnoticed flow of blood becomes a real possibility. So the default flips to טמאה, and she must be checked before handling pure items.

keyTerms.meaning: A presumption; the default status we assume
Their time of physical maturity
Presumed to be ritually pure
Presumed to be ritually impure
They check or examine

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
The presumption regarding Jewish girls is
that until they have reached their maturity
they are presumed pure,
and the women do not check them.
phrases.notes: The grown women check whether a girl is טהורה before she handles holy food or other pure items.

phrases.english: Once they have reached their maturity
they are presumed impure,
and the women check them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the discussion of the מדלפת closed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Before maturity a girl is in חזקת טהרה with no checking. After maturity she is in חזקת טומאה and must be checked.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: check them gently with oil, not by hand
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says not to check the girls by hand, because it can harm them. Instead the women smear oil inside and wipe outside, and any blood comes out on its own.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: They do not check them by hand, because that ruins them. Rather, they smear them with oil inside and wipe them outside, and they are checked by themselves.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה adds to the ברייתא. He does not dispute that the girls must be checked; he explains how to check them safely.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Checking by hand could scratch the girl. Then the blood from the scratch would make her look טמאה when she is not. Using oil avoids the scratch, and if she is ready to see blood, the oil helps it come out by itself.

keyTerms.meaning: They damage or ruin
They smear or anoint
They wipe off
They are checked on their own, without a hand check

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
They do not check them by hand,
because that ruins them,
phrases.notes: A hand check could scratch her, and then the blood would make her look טמאה.

phrases.english: rather they smear them with oil on the inside,
and wipe them on the outside,
and they are checked by themselves.
phrases.notes: If she is ready to see blood, the oil helps it flow out on its own.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: אֵין בּוֹדְקִין אוֹתָן בַּיָּד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a method of checking to the ruling of the ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Checking is done by smearing oil inside and wiping outside, not by hand.

steps.title: A reciter quotes רבי יוסי's ruling before רבי אלעזר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to רבי יוסי's statement in the משנה. A reciter quotes it before רבי אלעזר: a pregnant woman and a nursing woman who missed three cycles are טמאה only from the time she sees blood (דיה שעתה).
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי says: A pregnant woman, etc. A reciter taught before רבי אלעזר: רבי יוסי says: A pregnant woman and a nursing woman, if three cycles passed over her, her time is enough.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה and then a ברייתא version of רבי יוסי's ruling. This is setting up רבי אלעזר's question about the wording in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: דיה שעתה means she is טמאה only from the moment she sees, not backward in time. רבי יוסי gives this leniency after three cycles with no blood. Notice that the ruling starts with two women but uses singular words, 'over her' and 'her time.'

keyTerms.meaning: A pregnant woman
A nursing woman
Expected cycles or times when she would normally see blood
Her time is enough: she is טמאה only from when she sees, not retroactively

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says: A pregnant woman, etc.
A reciter taught before Rabbi Elazar:
phrases.notes: A תנא here is someone whose job was to recite ברייתות from memory.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says:
A pregnant woman and a nursing woman
for whom three cycles passed over her
her time is enough.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns from the ברייתא about girls to explain a line in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יוסי, a pregnant or nursing woman who missed three cycles is דיה שעתה.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר: you started with two women and ended with one
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר points out that the ברייתא mentions two women, pregnant and nursing, but then speaks in the singular ('her').
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: You opened with 'two' and finished with 'one'!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר challenges the wording of the ברייתא the reciter just quoted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the ruling covers two separate women, it should say 'over them' and 'their time.' The singular form suggests something is off, either in the text or in how we understand it.

keyTerms.meaning: You opened, began
You ended, finished
Two / one

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: רבי אלעזר is speaking to the reciter.

phrases.english: You opened with "two"
and you finished with "one"!
phrases.notes: The words עָלֶיהָ ('over her') and שְׁעָתָהּ ('her time') are singular.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the wording of the ברייתא quoted in the previous step.
steps.kashyaTarget: The wording of the ברייתא: 'pregnant and nursing' followed by singular forms.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A plural subject cannot fit with singular verbs and pronouns, so the text as read does not hang together.

steps.title: It means one woman who is pregnant and also nursing
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר suggests that the ברייתא speaks of one woman who is both pregnant and nursing. It then teaches in passing that her pregnancy days and nursing days combine.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps you are saying a pregnant woman who is also nursing. And it teaches us something along the way: her days of pregnancy count toward her days of nursing, and her days of nursing count toward her days of pregnancy.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר resolves his own question. The singular fits because the ברייתא is talking about just one woman.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Reading it as one woman fixes the grammar. It also yields a new law: the three missed cycles do not all need to fall in pregnancy or all in nursing. Cycles missed during pregnancy and cycles missed during nursing add up together.

keyTerms.meaning: Perhaps
A matter, a point
Along the way, in passing
It teaches us

steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean she nurses and is pregnant at the very same moment for the whole time. The point is that her pregnancy period and nursing period join together toward the three missed cycles.

phrases.english: Perhaps you are saying a pregnant woman who is also nursing,

phrases.aramaic: וּמִילְּתָא אַגַּב אוֹרְחֵיהּ קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן
phrases.english: and it teaches us a point along the way
that her days of pregnancy count for her
toward her days of nursing,

phrases.aramaic: וִימֵי מְנִיקוּתָהּ עוֹלִין לָהּ לִימֵי עִיבּוּרָהּ.
phrases.english: and her days of nursing count for her toward her days of pregnancy.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the wording challenge of the previous step.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of the subject: one woman with two conditions instead of two separate women.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא lists two separate women, which clashes with the singular wording.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is one woman who is pregnant and nursing, and her pregnancy days and nursing days combine toward the three cycles.
steps.whyThisMatters: It gives a practical rule: a woman may count missed cycles from pregnancy and nursing together to reach three.

steps.title: A ברייתא confirms that pregnancy and nursing days combine
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא supports רבי אלעזר's reading with a ברייתא that says the same thing word for word.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught: Her days of pregnancy count toward her days of nursing, and her days of nursing count toward her days of pregnancy.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to back up the new law that came out of רבי אלעזר's reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea that pregnancy and nursing days combine is not just a guess made to fix the grammar. A separate ברייתא states it outright, so the reading rests on a known teaching.

keyTerms.meaning: They count for her, they join in
Her days of pregnancy
Her days of nursing

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוסי's דיה שעתה applies after three missed cycles, and missed cycles during pregnancy and during nursing combine to make up the three.

phrases.english: As it is taught:

phrases.aramaic: יְמֵי עִיבּוּרָהּ עוֹלִין לָהּ לִימֵי מְנִיקוּתָהּ,
phrases.english: Her days of pregnancy count for her toward her days of nursing,

phrases.aramaic: וִימֵי מְנִיקוּתָהּ עוֹלִין לָהּ לִימֵי עִיבּוּרָהּ.
phrases.english: and her days of nursing count for her toward her days of pregnancy.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the law stated in the previous step.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that pregnancy days and nursing days combine toward the three cycles.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that states this rule explicitly.

steps.title: The ברייתא lists examples of cycles combining
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא gives three examples. In each one, missed cycles during pregnancy and missed cycles during nursing add up to three missed cycles.
steps.simpleTranslation: How does this work? She missed two cycles while pregnant and one while nursing; or two while nursing and one while pregnant; or one and a half while pregnant and one and a half while nursing. In each case they combine to make three cycles.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא that the גמרא brought as support in the last step continues. It now shows exactly how pregnancy days and nursing days join together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The point is that the three missed cycles do not all have to come from pregnancy or all from nursing. Any mix works, even a split of one and a half and one and a half. Once she reaches three, she counts as a woman whose דיה שעתה applies.

keyTerms.meaning: she stopped, meaning she went without seeing blood
her days of pregnancy
her days of nursing
they combine, they join together
expected cycles, the usual times she would see blood

phrases.english: How so?
If she stopped for two cycles during her days of pregnancy,
and one during her days of nursing;
or two during her days of nursing,
and one during her days of pregnancy;
or one and a half during her days of pregnancy,
and one and a half during her days of nursing
they combine to make three cycles.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes quoting the supporting ברייתא from step 20 by giving its examples.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Missed cycles from pregnancy and from nursing combine, in any split, to reach three cycles.

steps.title: How can nursing days count toward pregnancy days?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא accepts one direction of combining but asks how the other direction could ever happen.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense that pregnancy days count together with nursing days. That happens when she keeps nursing and then becomes pregnant. But nursing days counting together with pregnancy days, how can that happen?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא. One of its cases seems impossible in real life.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If she is nursing and becomes pregnant while still nursing, nothing breaks the streak, so the days easily join. In the other direction, a birth sits between the pregnancy and the nursing. A birth normally brings blood, so it should break the run of cycles without blood.

keyTerms.meaning: granted, it makes sense (accepting one part before attacking another)
they count for her, they are added in for her
how can you find such a case?

phrases.english: Granted, her days of pregnancy
count for her together with her days of nursing,
you can find it
where she keeps on nursing and then becomes pregnant,
phrases.notes: No birth comes in between here, so nothing interrupts her days without blood.

phrases.english: but her days of nursing
counting for her together with her days of pregnancy,
how can you find it?
phrases.notes: The worry is that a birth would come between the two, and a birth usually involves blood.

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא יְמֵי עִיבּוּרָהּ עוֹלִין לָהּ לִימֵי מְנִיקוּתָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks one of the examples the ברייתא just gave.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's case where nursing days combine with pregnancy days.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A birth between the pregnancy and the nursing should bring blood and break the streak, so the cycles could not combine.

steps.title: Three ways to explain the hard case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא offers three answers: a birth with no blood, birth blood that does not break the count, or simply removing that case.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want, say it is a dry birth. Or if you want, say menstrual blood is one thing and birth blood is another. Or if you want, say teach only one of the cases.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question with three separate options. You can pick any one of them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Answer one: the birth had no blood, so the streak was never broken. Answer two: birth blood is a different kind of blood from menstrual blood, so it does not stop the count of missed cycles. Answer three: the ברייתא should list only the easy direction and drop the hard one.

keyTerms.meaning: if you wish, say (introduces one possible answer out of several)
a dry birth, a birth with no blood
blood of giving birth
teach only one, take one case out of the ברייתא

steps.confusionAlert: These are three separate answers, not three steps of one answer. Each one fully solves the problem on its own.

phrases.english: If you wish, say: it is a dry birth,
phrases.notes: A "dry" birth is one with no blood, so it does not break her streak.

phrases.english: and if you wish, say:

phrases.aramaic: דַּם נִדָּה לְחוֹד וְדַם לֵידָה לְחוֹד,
phrases.english: menstrual blood is one thing and birth blood is another,
and if you wish, say: teach only one.
phrases.notes: He means: keep only the case where pregnancy days join nursing days, and drop the other one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 22.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Three alternative answers: change the case (dry birth), set a legal rule (birth blood does not count), or change the text (teach one).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The birth's blood breaks the streak, so nursing days could never join pregnancy days.
steps.terutzMaskana: Either the birth had no blood, or birth blood does not interrupt the count, or the ברייתא only teaches the easy direction.

steps.title: רב: the משנה's limit applies to all four women
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה, which limits דיה שעתה, and רב says this limit covers every woman in the list.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: "When did they say her time is enough..." and so on. רב said: this is about all of them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to the next line of the משנה. רב explains which cases that line refers to.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says that דיה שעתה applies only to the first time she sees blood. After that, she is treated like other women. רב rules that this limit applies to all four women in the משנה: the בתולה, the זקנה, the מעוברת and the מניקה. שמואל, in the next step, limits it to only some of them.

keyTerms.meaning: her time is enough: she is טמאה only from the moment she sees blood, not earlier
and so on, meaning the rest of the quoted line
on all of them

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב, דיה שעתה helps only on the first sighting, for every one of the four women in the משנה.

phrases.english: "In what case did they say her time is enough," etc.
phrases.notes: The rest of the line in the משנה: only for the first time she sees blood. The second time, she is like any other woman.

phrases.english: Rav said: this applies to all of them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the discussion of combining cycles and turns to the next line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The limit to the first sighting applies to all four women of the משנה.

steps.title: שמואל limits the rule to the virgin and the elderly woman
steps.stepSummary: שמואל disagrees with רב. He says the limit on דיה שעתה applies only to a בתולה and a זקנה. A pregnant or nursing woman keeps דיה שעתה for the whole time.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל says: The משנה's limit was taught only about a virgin and an elderly woman. But a pregnant woman and a nursing woman keep the leniency of 'her time is enough' for all the days of pregnancy and all the days of nursing.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל gives the opposite view to רב about which women the משנה's limit on דיה שעתה covers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב said the limit applies to all four women in the list. שמואל splits the list into two groups. For the בתולה and the זקנה the limit applies. The מעוברת and the מניקה keep דיה שעתה through the whole pregnancy and the whole nursing period, even if she sees blood more than once.

keyTerms.meaning: They taught this only about... (a phrase that narrows a rule)
Their time is enough. She is impure only from the moment she sees blood, not back in time.
Their days of pregnancy
Their days of nursing
A pregnant woman and a nursing woman

steps.confusionAlert: שמואל does not say the pregnant or nursing woman leaves the category of דיה שעתה. He says the opposite. Her leniency lasts longer, all through pregnancy or nursing, and the משנה's limit does not cut it short.

phrases.english: And Shmuel says:
They taught this only about a virgin and an elderly woman,
phrases.notes: 'This' means the limit in the line of the משנה that רב just said covers everyone.

phrases.english: but a pregnant woman and a nursing woman,
their time is enough for all the days of their pregnancy,
their time is enough for all the days of their nursing.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּשְׁמוּאֵל אָמַר: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא בְּתוּלָה וּזְקֵנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing view to רב's statement in step 24.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The limit on דיה שעתה applies only to the בתולה and the זקנה. The מעוברת and the מניקה keep דיה שעתה for the whole pregnancy and the whole nursing period.

steps.title: ריש לקיש and רבי יוחנן argue the same way
steps.stepSummary: The same argument shows up again. ריש לקיש holds like רב, that the limit covers everyone. רבי יוחנן holds like שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Likewise ריש לקיש says: The limit applies to all of them. רבי יוחנן says: It was taught only about a virgin and an elderly woman. But a pregnant or nursing woman keeps the leniency for all her days of pregnancy and all her days of nursing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that a second pair of אמוראים had the exact same argument as רב and שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש says 'אכולהו', the same word רב used, so he matches רב. רבי יוחנן repeats שמואל's words exactly. Nothing new is added to the law. We learn that this is a wider argument, not just one pair of rabbis.

keyTerms.meaning: And likewise. It introduces a matching statement.
On all of them. The limit covers every woman in the list.

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ:
phrases.english: And similarly Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish says:
It applies to all of them;
and Rabbi Yochanan says:
They taught this only about a virgin and an elderly woman,
but a pregnant woman and a nursing woman,
their time is enough for all the days of their pregnancy,
their time is enough for all the days of their nursing.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכֵן אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ: אַכּוּלְּהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the argument between רב and שמואל repeated by ריש לקיש and רבי יוחנן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ריש לקיש holds like רב, that the limit covers all the women. רבי יוחנן holds like שמואל, that it covers only the בתולה and the זקנה.

steps.title: Linking the argument to a dispute between תנאים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that this argument is the same as an argument between תנאים, and starts to quote a ברייתא about a pregnant or nursing woman.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is like a dispute between תנאים: A pregnant woman and a nursing woman who were...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move. It begins quoting a ברייתא where earlier sages, the תנאים, seem to argue the same point. The quote continues past this section.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'כתנאי' means the גמרא thinks the אמוראים are not inventing a new argument. They may be following two sides of an older argument among the תנאים. We will see in the coming lines whether the ברייתא really matches.

keyTerms.meaning: Like the תנאים. This argument matches an older argument among the sages of the משנה.
A teaching from the time of the תנאים that is not in the משנה

phrases.english: This is like a dispute between tannaim:
A pregnant woman and a nursing woman who were...

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proposes that the argument in steps 25 and 26 matches an argument between תנאים.
steps.raayaObject: The argument over whether the pregnant and nursing woman keep דיה שעתה for the whole period.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about a pregnant woman and a nursing woman. Its quote begins here and continues in the next lines.
